type:
∀ (X : Finset Nat) (r c : Nat) (A : Fin r → Finset ↥X) (B : Fin c → Finset ↥X),
  (∀ i, Finset.Nonempty (A i)) →
  (∀ j, Finset.Nonempty (B j)) →
  Pairwise (fun i i' => Disjoint (A i) (A i')) →
  Pairwise (fun j j' => Disjoint (B j) (B j')) →
  (∀ x : ↥X, ∃ i, x ∈ A i) →
  (∀ x : ↥X, ∃ j, x ∈ B j) →
  let G := Equiv.Perm ↥X
  let blockSym := fun S : Finset ↥X =>
    MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun x : ↥X => x ∈ S))
  let K : Subgroup G := iSup (fun i => blockSym (A i))
  let H : Subgroup G := iSup (fun j => blockSym (B j))
  ∀ σ : G,
    K ⊓ Subgroup.map (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj σ)) H =
      iSup (fun i => iSup (fun j =>
        blockSym (A i ∩ Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding σ) (B j))))
sourceReason: Ian Xiao, § 7.2, after Proposition 7.3, p. 30. The published PDF matches the project copy. The supplied defect report returned HTTP 404, and no correction for this endpoint was available in the task context. The covering partitions include the singleton blocks. Fin indices encode the chosen block orders, and points inherit the natural order on Nat. Every permutation represents its own double coset. The subgroup suprema give the products of disjoint block factors, each extended by the identity on its complement in X. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf
